summary.headline: Platinum Industries Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR 108.9 crore (from INR 115.4 crore) and PAT to INR 11.13 crore as Palghar ramp-up weighed.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue declined about 5.6% YoY to INR 108.9 crore while EBITDA fell to INR 13.44 crore at a 12.34% margin, versus INR 15.16 crore at 13.14% a year earlier. Standalone revenue grew about 7.3% YoY to INR 110.4 crore, but standalone EBITDA margin was 11.64%. The expanded Palghar facility only became fully operational on 21 May 2026, so the quarter carried ramp-up costs and lower lead-free PVC offtake. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% and kept Egypt commercial production targeted before 31 December 2026.

segments.name: CPVC additives
segments.commentary: Margin currently about 18% against a target of 20-21% by Q4 FY27, which management says depends on demand recovery and local raw material sourcing. Gross margin in CPVC has risen from 6-7% to 17-18%, per management.

segments.name: Lead-free PVC additives
segments.commentary: Q1 offtake was lower, which management cited as the main reason for the margin decline because this is a high-margin product. Management names Baerlocher and Reagens as main competitors in lead-free.

segments.name: Oleo chemicals (Platinum Oleo Chemicals)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR 5.3 crore. FY27 target of INR 65-70 crore per management, with INR 150-200 crore targeted over three years. Seed marketing is via CDMO, with exports to Malaysia and Turkey, and own manufacturing is planned in about 1.5 years.

segments.name: Rivadu Lifesciences (pharma)
segments.commentary: Business model still being defined. Some revenue began this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of 30-40% reiterated, though management said the Egypt contribution is now lower than earlier planned.
Egypt revenue for FY27 cut to INR 30-35 crore from an earlier INR 50-60 crore estimate.
EBITDA margin guidance of 13-15% and PAT margin of 11-12% for coming months, reaffirmed from the previous call.
Egypt plant (60,000 tpa, about INR 67-68 crore capex) to start commercial production before 31 December 2026; Egypt top line of INR 250-300 crore over three years.
Palghar expansion peak potential of INR 700-800 crore over three years; top-line CAGR of about 35% over three years.
Stearates plant (6,000 tpa) now expected September/October 2026 versus earlier August, due to an equipment delay.
Oleo FY27 revenue INR 65-70 crore (management), vs analyst question of INR 55-60 crore; management said it was 'very positive'.
capex_capacity: Palghar expansion (~60,000 tpa: 24,000 tpa lead-free PVC, 24,000 tpa CPVC, 12,000 tpa lubricants and others) commenced commercial production 21 May 2026; CPVC partial operations from August 2025. Palghar capex about INR 71 crore.
Total Indian capacity expected to reach 85,000+ tpa on full ramp-up of the expanded facility.
Utilisation of the new capacity expected at around 30-35% in Q2-Q3 FY27, per CFO.
Egypt plant (60,000 tpa; mainly lead stabilisers) capex about INR 67 crore (management also cited a total of ~INR 68 crore). Commercial production targeted before 31 December 2026.
Stearates plant (6,000 tpa) delayed to September/October 2026 due to equipment delay. Oleo manufacturing plant planned in about 1.5 years; land already acquired.
demand_pricing: Pipe demand degrew in Q1 across pipe companies, per management; demand has picked up from August and management expects good demand through December as PVC prices stabilised and turned upward.
CPVC: a demand-supply gap exists with supply exceeding demand, so the company pushed sales in Q1. Management expects margin recovery only in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

Raw material supply disrupted by shipping and war-related freight costs; some raw materials bought locally, which pressured margins. Management says the company cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs in this environment.
Management said pricing is not under pressure: competitors and the company 'understand the same pricing levels'. Competitors in lead-free: Baerlocher, Reagens; Goldstab mainly lead-based.

Lubrizol/Aditya Birla CPVC resin capacity, plus Reliance and Meghmani resin plans, described by management as complementary to its CPVC additives business. Supply to Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years.
Sales-related expenses fell sharply as the company skipped exhibitions in Q1; ECL provisions were also lower.

qa_highlights.question: How did pipe demand look in July and August, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pipe demand degrew in Q1 across pipe companies, picked up from August, and is expected to stay good through December as PVC prices stabilised and turned upward.

qa_highlights.question: What were Oleo sales in Q1 FY27 and can the segment reach INR 55-60 crore by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Oleo revenue was about INR 5.3 crore. Management said it is 'very positive' on the year-end target; the analyst's INR 55-60 crore figure was not confirmed, and the INR 65-70 crore FY27 target was given later in the call.

qa_highlights.question: When will CPVC margins recover toward 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: CPVC margin is about 18% now and management targets 20-21% by Q4 FY27. Recovery depends on demand, since supply currently exceeds demand, and on local raw material sourcing, which is adding cost.

qa_highlights.question: Volume, price and mix split, new customers, and stabilizer versus specialty volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product volume data and suggested the analyst connect offline.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA margin is structural versus temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower sales-related expenses, since the company skipped exhibitions in Q1, and lower ECL provisions offset the drop in contribution margin, leaving EBITDA margin impact negligible. Lead-free PVC offtake was lower, which hurt mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation of the existing stabilizer capacity and the threshold to sustain margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The expanded plant was fully operational only from 21 May 2026, so utilisation is expected to be around 30-35% in Q2 and Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-off items in other income or forex in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: A forex gain of about INR 1 crore was reflected in other income.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-40% still maintained, and how much Egypt revenue is included?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 30-40% growth for FY27 and said the company is already on track, though demand was weak due to the war. Egypt is only partly included: FY27 Egypt estimate is cut to INR 30-35 crore from INR 50-60 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Oleo revenue potential over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Oleo target is INR 65-70 crore and the three-year target is INR 150-200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Lubrizol and Aditya Birla CPVC resin capacity on Platinum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resin capacity is complementary, since additives are about 25% of a CPVC compound and resin about 75%. The company has supplied Supreme and Prince Pipes for 1-2 years, and the transition will take time.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure in lead-free and CPVC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct CPVC additive competition in India apart from one other Indian company. In lead-free, Baerlocher and Reagens are the main competitors, Goldstab is mainly lead-based, and pricing levels are understood by all players.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook versus the roughly 23% margins of FY23-FY24?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the change to a mix shift from high-margin lead-free to lower-margin CPVC, which started at a 3-7% contribution margin. Guidance is PAT margin of 11-12% and EBITDA margin of 13-15%, reiterated from the previous call.

qa_highlights.question: Project-wise capex, timelines and revenue potential for Egypt and Palghar?
qa_highlights.answer: Egypt is expected by December 2026, with INR 250-300 crore top line over three years. Palghar peak potential is INR 700-800 crore over three years, and top-line CAGR is about 35% over three years.

qa_highlights.question: What bottlenecks could delay commissioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not expect much delay.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the stearates plant and its effect on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6,000 tpa stearates plant has slipped to September/October 2026 from August due to a delay in one equipment item. Management said it would not materially affect FY27 revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Rivadu Lifesciences pharma and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Business model is still being defined. Some revenue started this quarter, with collaborations with overseas companies under negotiation. No figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material inflation pass-through and contractual mechanisms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can pass on raw material price rises in normal conditions, but in the current war and shipping environment it cannot pass on sudden freight, CFS and transport costs. Lower lead-free PVC offtake was cited as the main Q1 margin driver.

qa_highlights.question: Egypt versus Palghar capex and why revenue potential differs?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 67 crore for Egypt and INR 71 crore for Palghar. Both have about 60,000 tpa capacity, but Egypt is mainly lead stabilisers, priced at INR 110-150 per kg versus INR 250-300 for CPVC and INR 170-220 for calcium zinc in India.

qa_highlights.question: Incremental working capital needed for Egypt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly a three-month working capital cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Expected margins in Oleo chemicals in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are expected to rise after the company builds its own manufacturing facility; for now it is using CDMO for seed marketing.

risks_watch: CPVC margin recovery to 20-21% is pinned to Q3-Q4 FY27 and depends on demand that management says has only just picked up from August.
Palghar utilisation of around 30-35% in Q2-Q3 FY27 is low against a capacity expansion of about 60,000 tpa, so fixed costs and depreciation may keep margins under pressure.
Egypt FY27 revenue guidance was cut to INR 30-35 crore from INR 50-60 crore, and the plant must start commercial production before 31 December 2026.
Stearates plant has slipped to September/October 2026, and any further equipment delay would extend the timeline.
Freight, CFS and transport costs from the war and shipping disruptions cannot be fully passed through, and some raw materials are now bought locally at higher cost.
Oleo FY27 target of INR 65-70 crore is well above Q1 revenue of about INR 5.3 crore, and the analyst's INR 55-60 crore figure was not confirmed by management.
key_quotes: The first quarter of FY27 was a period of transition and capacity ramp-up for the company.
So, right now, we are on 18%, we wish to be on 20%, 21% by the fourth quarter.
We will be maintaining a PAT margin of 11%, 12% in the coming months.
So, there is no threat as such. In fact, we are going to complement each other in terms of the growth.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth and the 30-40% FY27 revenue guidance, but cautious on near-term margins and demand, attributing Q1 weakness to ramp-up, product mix, freight costs and weak pipe demand. It was evasive on volume, price and mix splits, declining to share product volume data and referring the analyst offline.
